Example Program: LEDs

This folder contains an example application for the Winford Engineering
ETH32 ethernet I/O device.  

OVERVIEW:
This is a very simple program that provides an example of how to 
connect to the ETH32 and alter the status of its two built-in LEDs.
No I/O pin connections are necessary for this example.  This example 
is perfect for trying out the ETH32 "right out of the box."

This example also includes the ability to detect ETH32 devices on the 
local network, and thus provides a simple example of using the Detection 
capabilities of the ETH32 API.


OPERATION:
Click the Detect button to populate the combo box with the IP addresses 
of any ETH32 devices found on the local network.  After the device(s) 
have been detected, choose one, or if the device is not on the local network, 
you can manually enter the IP address or host name 
of the ETH32 device you would like to connect to.  This example allows 
the device's LEDs to be turned on and off from your computer.

PROGRAMMING LANGUAGES:
This sample application is included in these programming languages:
  * Visual Basic 6
  * Visual C# .NET
